data.title: Chancroid — viva
data.summary: Sexually transmitted infections · 10 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Chancroid** (Sexually transmitted infections)_

**Q1. What is chancroid? Organism?**
- Acute STI with painful genital ulcers and suppurative inguinal lymphadenitis caused by Haemophilus ducreyi — small Gram-negative coccobacillus
- Now rare in India (declined with syndromic management); also causes non-sexual chronic leg ulcers in the tropics/Pacific (yaws-like settings)

**Q2. Pathogenic factors of H. ducreyi (PYQ).**
- Entry through micro-abrasions; cytolethal distending toxin (cell-cycle arrest, apoptosis), haemolysin, outer-membrane proteins (DsrA serum resistance, LspA anti-phagocytic), pili; incubation 3–7 days

**Q3. Describe the ulcer.**
- Starts as tender papule → pustule → ulcer in 1–2 days
- Ulcer: painful, soft (not indurated — 'soft sore'), ragged undermined edges, purulent grey-yellow necrotic base that bleeds easily, surrounding erythema; often multiple ('kissing ulcers' by autoinoculation)
- Sites: men — prepuce, frenulum, coronal sulcus; women — fourchette, labia (women may be asymptomatic carriers)

**Q4. Describe the bubo of chancroid.**
- Painful unilateral inguinal lymphadenitis in ~50%, 1–2 weeks after ulcer; matted, fluctuant, may rupture forming a single sinus/ulcer ('bubonulus')
- Overlying skin red; rupture can produce large inguinal ulcers

**Q5. Clinical variants.**
- Giant chancroid, serpiginous chancroid, phagedenic chancroid (destructive with secondary anaerobes), follicular, dwarf (small superficial), transient (heals then bubo — mimics LGV), papular (mimics donovanosis/condyloma lata)
- Mixed chancre — chancroid + syphilis together (rolled induration appearing later)

**Q6. Complications of chancroid (PYQ).**
- Phimosis/paraphimosis, phagedena (tissue destruction), fistula, urethral stricture, bubo rupture and large ulcer
- Increased HIV acquisition and transmission (ulcer breaches mucosa), mixed infection with syphilis

**Q7. Diagnostic tests (PYQ).**
- Gram stain of ulcer edge/bubo pus: Gram-negative coccobacilli in parallel chains — 'school of fish' or 'railroad track' (low sensitivity)
- Culture on enriched selective media (Nairobi/Mueller–Hinton chocolate agar with vancomycin, 33 °C, CO2) — sensitivity <80%
- Multiplex PCR (H. ducreyi, T. pallidum, HSV) — test of choice
- Exclude syphilis (dark-field, serology at baseline and 3 months) and herpes; HIV test
- CDC probable diagnosis: painful ulcer(s), no T. pallidum evidence, typical lymphadenopathy, HSV test negative

**Q8. Differentiate chancroid from syphilitic chancre.**
- Chancroid: incubation 3–7 days, multiple, painful, soft, ragged undermined edge, dirty bleeding base, painful suppurating unilateral bubo
- Chancre: 9–90 days, usually single, painless, indurated (button-like), clean base with serous exudate, rubbery painless bilateral non-suppurating nodes

**Q9. Treatment.**
- Azithromycin 1 g single oral dose OR ceftriaxone 250 mg IM single dose OR ciprofloxacin 500 mg twice daily for 3 days OR erythromycin base 500 mg thrice daily for 7 days
- NACO syndromic: white kit (benzathine penicillin + azithromycin) for non-herpetic ulcer, blue kit if penicillin allergy; black kit for bubo
- Fluctuant bubo: needle aspiration through healthy skin or incision and drainage — do not excise
- Treat partners in last 10 days; review at 3–7 days (ulcers improve symptomatically in 3 days, heal in ~7–14 days)

**Q10. Why is chancroid less common now?**
- Syndromic management, condom promotion, antibiotics for GUD, sex-worker programmes — WHO considers it nearly eliminated in many regions

## Quick spotter facts
- Painful soft ragged ulcer with dirty base + suppurating bubo — chancroid
- School-of-fish on Gram stain
- Treat with azithromycin 1 g single dose

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Chancroid); NACO National Technical Guidelines on RTI/STI (syndromic management, colour-coded kits). Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
